Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $A\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}$ be fixed, let $k\ge2$, $p\ge2$ be integers
with $\ell=k+p\le\min(m,n)$, and draw $\Omega\in\mathbb C^{n\times\ell}$
with iid normalized complex Gaussian entries satisfying $\mathbb E|g|^2=1$.
Let $Q$ be the exact finite-scan range-finder basis of
$\operatorname{Ran}(A\Omega)$ returned by
[[alg-gaussian-randomized-range-finder]], and put $P=QQ^*$. Then
$$\mathbb E\|(I-P)A\|_2\le\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{p}}\,\sigma_{k+1} +\frac{e\sqrt\ell}{p}\left(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
In particular, the original approved bound with leading coefficient
$1+\sqrt{k/(p-1)}$ follows. The algorithm and sketch width $\ell$ are
unchanged; only the analysis may use a larger SVD partition rank.

interface_changes.before:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice so that the repository's Lebesgue measure
on each finite-dimensional real coordinate space is a measure. A **standard
real Gaussian scalar** has Lebesgue density
$$\varphi_R(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}.$$
A **normalized complex Gaussian scalar** is $z=(x+iy)/\sqrt2$ for independent
standard real Gaussian scalars $x,y$; its density on $\mathbb C\simeq\mathbb
R^2$ is $\varphi_C(z)=\pi^{-1}e^{-|z|^2}$ and $\mathbb E|z|^2=1$.

For $F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, an **iid standard Gaussian matrix** in
$F^{a\times b}$ has independent entries with the corresponding scalar law.
All its expectations are finite-dimensional Lebesgue integrals against the
product density. Independence means this product-density factorization.
The normalized complex convention is fixed throughout; it is not the
unnormalized law $x+iy$.
interface_changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice so that the repository's Lebesgue measure
on each positive-dimensional real coordinate space is a measure. A **standard
real Gaussian scalar** has Lebesgue density
$$\varphi_R(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}.$$
A **normalized complex Gaussian scalar** is $z=(x+iy)/\sqrt2$ for independent
standard real Gaussian scalars $x,y$; its density on $\mathbb C\simeq\mathbb
R^2$ is $\varphi_C(z)=\pi^{-1}e^{-|z|^2}$ and $\mathbb E|z|^2=1$.

For $F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, an **iid standard Gaussian matrix** in
$F^{a\times b}$ has independent entries with the corresponding scalar law.
For $ab>0$, its expectations are finite-dimensional Lebesgue integrals
against the product density. If $a=0$ or $b=0$, the matrix space has one
element, the empty matrix; its law assigns that element probability one,
and the expectation of any function is its value there. Independence means
the product-density factorization, with this one-point convention for an
empty product.
The normalized complex convention is fixed throughout; it is not the
unnormalized law $x+iy$.

interface_changes.before:
Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $(\Xi,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)$ be a
probability space, let $A\in F^{m\times n}$ be fixed, let $\ell\ge1$ be an
integer, and let $q\ge0$ be an integer. Let $\Omega:\Xi\to F^{n\times\ell}$
be measurable and let $P:\Xi\to F^{m\times m}$ be a measurable orthogonal
projector-valued map whose value $P(\xi)$ projects onto the output range of the procedure in
[[alg-randomized-power-subspace-iteration-with-qr]] applied to $A,\Omega(\xi),q$.
Assume
$$\mathbb E\|(I-P)(AA^*)^qA\|_2<\infty,$$
where expectation is with respect to $\mathbb P$. Then
$$\mathbb E\|(I-P)A\|_2\le \left(\mathbb E\|(I-P)(AA^*)^qA\|_2\right)^{1/(2q+1)}.$$
This is a transfer inequality; it assumes the powered error expectation has
already been bounded.
